title: Grateful Dead Live at Frost Amphitheatre on 1982-10-10
lineage: Cassette (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby C) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/48k) -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.1 -> FLAC/24
source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90/Dolby B) -> Cassette (JVC KD-V6/XLII-S90/Dolby C)

ai_review.summary: Superb 24‑bit soundboard captures a high‑energy 1982 Frost show highlighted by Brent’s fiery organ, Jerry’s soaring guitar and standout performances of Sugaree, Crazy Fingers, Touch of Grey and Black Peter.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean 24‑bit SBD with excellent clarity despite a few early balance quirks and a faint hiss. Musically the night bursts with energy – Brent’s organ solo on Minglewood, Jerry’s top‑form guitar work, Phil’s prominent bass, and Bob’s vocal flourishes make for a memorable set that deadheads cite as a classic Frost performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 5) and enthusiastic comments about both the musical performance and the soundboard quality; minor technical hiccups keep it just shy of “exceptional.”

recording_quality.technical_notes: 24‑bit SBD praised as crisp and sweet, with a ‘dirty and grindy’ character the reviewer loves. Early balance issues in Minglewood are quickly corrected; a slight hiss and some missing frequency detail noted, but overall very listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong opening with Minglewood and Rooster, smooth transition into a tight first set that builds through Cassidy and China>Rider. Second set lifts further with Playing in the Band → Crazy Fingers → Touch of Grey, ending on an uplifting double encore of Satisfaction and It's All Over Now, Baby Blue.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as ‘on top of his game’ with a nice guitar tone, added gain for solos, and delivering powerful leads throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted as prominent and present; bass is loud and driving, especially noticeable in the early songs and during transitions.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals receive praise – extra verse on Rooster, spoken‑word flourishes, and ‘cheese points’ for his lyrical improvisations.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s organ work is called ‘on fire,’ with a standout solo on Minglewood and key contributions to jams like Far From Me and Crazy Fingers.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drummers are noted as ‘on fire’ closing the set, providing a strong, powerful outro that lifts the energy of the final songs.
